data.one_liner: An HTTP/2 implementation in Dart for low-level transport and pooled HTTP/2 requests.
data.what_it_does: Provides an HTTP/2 interface on top of a bidirectional stream of bytes, allowing raw HTTP/2 communication as well as a pooled `http.Client` implementation that multiplexes requests over shared connections.
use_when: You need to make concurrent requests multiplexed over a shared HTTP/2 connection
You are implementing low-level HTTP/2 clients or servers in Dart
You need a `package:http` Client backed exclusively by HTTP/2
avoid_when: You need automatic fallback to HTTP/1.1 for servers that do not support HTTP/2
You just want a simple high-level REST client without dealing with transport streams
strengths: Supports multiplexing multiple requests over a single connection
Provides fine-grained control over frames, streams, and transport connections
weaknesses: Does not fall back to HTTP/1.1 if a server fails to negotiate HTTP/2
Requires handling low-level byte streams and header framing for custom requests

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a standard high-level HTTP client supporting HTTP/1.1 and standard workflows.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a feature-rich HTTP client with interceptors, global configuration, and form data support.
